paid_money.title: I already paid money to scammers
paid_money.response:
If you’ve paid money to scammers, take these steps immediately:

1. **Contact Your Bank or Payment Provider:** Notify them about the fraudulent transaction. They may be able to reverse the payment or stop further charges.
2. **Report to Authorities:** File a report with your local law enforcement and the FTC at https://reportfraud.ftc.gov.
3. **Monitor Your Accounts:** Check your bank and credit card statements for any unauthorized charges.
4. **Change Passwords:** If you shared any login details, change your passwords immediately.

For more details, visit: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/what-do-if-you-were-scammed

get_money_back.title: How to get my money back
get_money_back.response:
Getting your money back after a scam can be challenging, but here’s what you can do:

1. **Contact Your Bank:** Ask if they can reverse the transaction (e.g., for credit card payments or wire transfers).
2. **File a Complaint:** Report the scam to the FTC at https://reportfraud.ftc.gov.
3. **Check for Refund Policies:** If you paid through a platform like PayPal, check their refund policies.
4. **Seek Legal Advice:** Consult a lawyer to explore your options.

Learn more at: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/what-do-if-you-were-scammed

prevent_scams.title: How to avoid scams in the future
prevent_scams.response:
To protect yourself from scams:

1. **Be Skeptical:** If an offer sounds too good to be true, it probably is.
2. **Verify Contacts:** Double-check the identity of anyone asking for money or personal information.
3. **Use Secure Payment Methods:** Avoid wire transfers or gift cards for payments.
4. **Stay Informed:** Regularly check scam alerts from the FTC at https://consumer.ftc.gov/scam-alerts.

For more tips, visit: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-avoid-scam

identity_theft.title: What to do if my identity was stolen
identity_theft.response:
If you suspect identity theft, take these steps:

1. **Place a Fraud Alert:** Contact one of the three major credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, or TransUnion) to place a fraud alert on your credit report.
2. **Check Your Credit Report:** Look for any unauthorized accounts or transactions.
3. **Report to the FTC:** File a report at https://identitytheft.gov.
4. **Contact Financial Institutions:** Notify your bank, credit card companies, and other financial institutions.

Learn more at: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/what-do-if-your-identity-stolen

phishing_scam.title: What to do if I fell for a phishing scam
phishing_scam.response:
If you’ve fallen for a phishing scam, act quickly:

1. **Change Passwords:** Update passwords for any compromised accounts.
2. **Enable Two-Factor Authentication:** Add an extra layer of security to your accounts.
3. **Scan for Malware:** Run a virus scan on your device to check for malware.
4. **Report the Scam:** Forward phishing emails to reportphishing@apwg.org and report to the FTC at https://reportfraud.ftc.gov.

For more details, visit: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-recognize-and-avoid-phishing-scams

job_scam.title: What to do if I fell for a job scam
job_scam.response:
If you’ve been scammed by a fake job offer, take these steps:

1. **Stop Communication:** Do not provide any more personal information or money.
2. **Report the Scam:** File a complaint with the FTC at https://reportfraud.ftc.gov.
3. **Contact Your Bank:** If you paid any fees, ask if they can reverse the transaction.
4. **Warn Others:** Share your experience to help others avoid similar scams.

Learn more at: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/job-scams

romance_scam.title: What to do if I fell for a romance scam
romance_scam.response:
If you’ve been scammed in a romance scam, take these steps:

1. **Stop Communication:** Cut off all contact with the scammer.
2. **Report the Scam:** File a complaint with the FTC at https://reportfraud.ftc.gov.
3. **Contact Your Bank:** If you sent money, ask if they can reverse the transaction.
4. **Seek Support:** Talk to friends, family, or a counselor for emotional support.

For more details, visit: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/what-you-need-know-about-romance-scams

tech_support_scam.title: What to do if I fell for a tech support scam
tech_support_scam.response:
If you’ve been scammed by a fake tech support call or website, take these steps:

1. **Disconnect Your Device:** If you gave remote access, disconnect your device from the internet.
2. **Scan for Malware:** Run a virus scan to check for any installed malware.
3. **Change Passwords:** Update passwords for any compromised accounts.
4. **Report the Scam:** File a complaint with the FTC at https://reportfraud.ftc.gov.

Learn more at: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-spot-avoid-and-report-tech-support-scams
